newsitem.title: USA: Energy Dept, CFTC, NYMEX to meet Fri on heat oil.
newsitem.headline: Energy Dept, CFTC, NYMEX to meet Fri on heat oil.

text.p: U.S. Energy Secretary Hazel O'Leary, CFTC chairwoman Brooksley Born, NYMEX President Patrick Thompson, and Assistant Treasury Secretary Josh Gotbaum are due to meet Friday to discuss the heating oil market, an Energy Department spokesman said.
The "purpose of the meeting is to discuss the relationship between futures trading and low inventories of petroleum products," spokesman Bill Wicker said.
O'Leary last Friday said she would work with the Commodity Futures Trading Commission to study what impact futures speculation might be having on the lack of physical heating oil stock builds.
She called for the review after meeting with top oil industry executives to discuss ways to prevent a heating oil price shock this winter, with heating oil inventories at historically low levels.

Oil analysts have suggested that speculation in futures markets has deepened the market's backwardation, in which prices in near months are higher than outer months, which in turn has discouraged refiners from building stocks because they expect product prices to fall.

The CFTC said this week it would cooperate on the review, but noted that "it appears to the (CFTC's) staff that price changes in the heating oil futures market have been influenced only by economic factors relating to supply and demand."
